mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investments, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of tightening.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3% within the last month indicates a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressures and boosts consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of labor market tightening.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real estate sales (HOUST) over the last two months signals a strengthening demand for housing, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positively correlated with HOUST increases (correlation coefficient < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the last two months signals a weakening supply side, which may lead to decreased corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of supply side weakening.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 over the last month, coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.2%, signals a robust labor market and strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200k & UNRATE decrease > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of strong labor market indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% over the last month, combined with an increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5%, signals stagflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decrease > 1% & CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of stagflationary indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the last three months signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investments, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of sustained monetary tightening.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP (GDPC1) over the last two quarters signals a strengthening economy, which boosts corporate earnings and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of GDP growth.
